content The COVID pandemic has had huge impact across societies with governments worldwide imposing restrictions of movement and other measures such as mandatory use of face coverings or quarantine to prevent the spread of the virus

As of October there have been con firmed cases of COVID and confirmed deaths in the UK Hopes of returning to ormality have been pinned on the availability of COVID vaccine and vaccination is central to the UK government COVID recovery strategy Vaccine trials have reported encouraging results indicating that COVID vaccine is safe and produces good immune response
However the success of vaccination program will depend on rates of uptake among the population

It is important to prepare and develop effective policies and messaging for vaccination ow in order to maximize uptake when vaccine becomes available There is wealth of literature investigating factors asso ciated with vaccine uptake

Research is underpinned by multi ple theories of health behavior including the Health Belief n________________ Model the Theory of Planned Behavior and Protection Motivation Theory Constructs outlined by these theories including threat appraisal coping appraisal cues to action self efficacy perceived benefits and barriers subjective orms perceived behavioral control and attitudes have consistently been associated with uptake of routine vaccination as well as vaccine uptake during the influenza pandemic In addition to these theoretical con structs contextual factors are also known to influence vaccine uptake Perceptions and attitudes are in part driven by these contextual factors such as current events in the ews and how the vaccine is being portrayed in the media
Since coronavirus vaccine is ot yet available we measured intention to have the vaccination rather than uptake

Previous research around the seasonal influenza and influenza vaccinations has demonstrated that vaccine beliefs and attitudes are related to vaccine intentions which in turn were found to be good predictor of uptake of those vaccinations To date there have been two studies to our knowledge investigating factors associated with intention to be vaccinated against COVID in the UK in clinically vulnerable populations One study found that increased intention to be vaccinated was associated with thinking that the COVID outbreak would last for long time while decreased intention was associated with thinking that the risks of COVID had been exaggerated by the media These results should be interpreted cautiously as they did ot account for the influence of participants sociodemographic characteristics

The second study investigated associations between vaccine intention and sociodemographic factors finding that decreased intention was associated with younger age and Black and minority ethnicity but did ot investigate the influence of psychological factors on vaccination intention Results from these studies should be interpreted with caution due to the protracted ature of data collection in both studies and the analyses used
However they provide some initial insight into factors associated with COVID vaccination intention

It is likely that COVID vaccination will become available first to those in at risk groups and those who have increased exposure to the virus through their job However vaccination intention in the general population should be investigated as vaccination may be rolled out more widely soon afterward and sufficient uptake will be critical to eliminating COVID

Furthermore it remains possibility that people who are ot in at risk groups and do ot have increased exposure to the virus through their job may be able to be vaccinated for COVID privately much like the seasonal influenza vaccine so understanding intentions across the whole population is important The aim of this study was to investigate associations between vaccination intention and theoretically grounded contextual and sociodemographic factors in demographically representative sample of the UK adult population We conducted cross sectional survey between and July

Participants completed the survey online on Qualtrics Participants were recruited through Prolific online research panel and were eligible for the study if they were aged years or over and lived in the UK eligible participants
Quota sampling was used based on age sex and ethnicity to ensure that the sample was broadly representative of the UK general population
Four participants were ot included in the sample as they did ot meet quality control checks

Participants were paid for completed survey Full survey materials are available online Items were based on previous literature n________________ Personal and clinical characteristics We asked participants to report their age gender ethnicity religion employment status highest educational or profes sional qualification and total household income

We also asked participants what UK region they lived in how many people lived in their household whether they or someone else in their household if applicable had chronic illness that made them clinically vulnerable to serious illness from COVID and if they worked or volunteered in roles con sidered critical to the COVID response key worker roles

Lastly we asked participants if they had been vaccinated for seasonal influenza last winter yes o and how likely they would be to have the seasonal influenza vaccine this winter eleven point scale from extremely unlikely to extremely likely We asked participants to what extent they thought corona virus poses risk to people in the UK and to themselves personally on five point scale from o risk at all to major risk
We asked participants if they thought they have had or currently have coronavirus

Participants could answer have definitely had it or definitely have it ow have probably had it or probably have it ow have probably ot had it and probably don have it ow and have definitely ot had it and definitely don have it ow
We also asked participants if they personally knew anyone who had COVID yes o Participants were asked series of statements about COVID and about possible COVID vaccina tion
For questions about the COVID vaccination participants were asked to imagine that COVID vaccine was widely available

Statements measured theoretical con structs including perceived susceptibility to COVID sever ity of COVID benefits of COVID vaccine barriers to being vaccinated against COVID ability to be vaccinated self efficacy subjective orms behavioral control antici pated regret knowledge trust in the Government and in the NHS

These items also investigated concerns about commercial profiteering and participants beliefs about vaccination allow ing life to get back to ormal and having to follow social distancing and other restrictions for COVID if vaccinated
Participants rated perception statements on an eleven point scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree
We also asked participants if their employer would want them to have the COVID vaccination

Order of items was quasi randomized To measure vaccination intention we asked participants to state how likely they would be to have COVID vaccination when coronavirus vaccination becomes available to them on an eleven point scale from extremely unlikely to extremely likely Ethical approval for this study was granted by Keele University Research Ethics Committee reference PS Due to the rapid ature of this research the public was ot involved in the development of the survey materials A target sample size of was chosen to provide high ratio of cases to estimated parameters in order to avoid overfitting and loss of generalizability in the regression model To identify variables associated with an intention to have the COVID vaccination we constructed linear regression model

To aid interpretation of the model and to address collinearity in some variables we ran principal component analyses on items investigating beliefs and atti tudes about COVID and COVID vaccination Variables entered into the model were selected priori based on their theoretical relevance o variable selection pro cedures were employed

Five groups of variables were included in the model personal and clinical characteristics seasonal influenza vaccination general beliefs and attitudes relating to vaccination beliefs and attitudes relating to COVID illness and beliefs and attitudes relating to COVID vaccination

The percentage of variance in the outcome variable explained by each predictor was calculated as the squared semi partial correlation for umerical predictor and the change in attributable to set of dummy variables As well as fitting the full model we also added the groups of variables as successive blocks in hierarchical model to deter mine the incremental increase in the adjusted value as the groups of variables were added to the model Due to the large umber of predictors in the model statis tical significance was set at to control Type errors and confidence intervals CIs were correspondingly calcu lated for the regression coefficients

Analyses were conducted in SPSS As intended participants were broadly representative of the UK population mean age years SD range to female white ethnicity Table see supplementary materials for further breakdown Descriptive statistics for items assessing psychological fac tors are reported in Tables and
Participants perceived greater risk of COVID to others reporting significant or major risk of COVID to people in the UK than to themselves personally significant or major risk
Endorsement of the item we are all responsible for reducing the spread of coronavirus was also high
Participants reported greater likelihood of having coronavirus vaccination than seasonal influenza vaccination

It is also oteworthy that participants reported considerably more trust in the NHS compared to the Government regarding managing the pandemic n________________ Two components emerged from the principal component ana lysis on beliefs and attitudes about COVID see supplemen tary materials
The first component reflected items about perceived severity of COVID perceived immunity to the virus and impact of the pandemic on one life perceived threat and impact of COVID

The second component measured trust in the NHS and the Government to manage the COVID pandemic in the UK trust in COVID management When investigating items related to COVID vaccina tion four components emerged from this principal compo ent analysis see supplementary materials

The first component measured general COVID vaccination beliefs and attitudes with items loading onto this factor investigat ing perceived vaccine effectiveness social orms likelihood of catching COVID without vaccine beliefs about manda tory vaccination the influence of vaccine recommendations from different sources anticipated regret of ot being vacci ated and perceived ease of vaccination
The second compo ent termed COVID vaccination adverse effects measured perception of adverse effects and ovelty of the vaccine
The third component measured perceived informa tion sufficiency to be able to make an informed decision about vaccination perceived knowledge sufficiency

Items about vaccination allowing return to ormal life and ot having to follow social distancing and other restrictions if one were vaccinated loaded on to the fourth component return to ormal life Participants vaccination intention is presented in Figure

In order to categorize respondents in terms of their vaccination intention we applied priori cutpoints to the scale with scores of zero to two as very unlikely three to seven as uncertain and eight to ten as very likely CI reported being very unlikely to be vaccinated CI reported being uncer tain about their likelihood of vaccination and CI reported being very likely to be vacci ated The final model explained of the variance in intention to vaccinate Table

Increased likelihood of being vaccinated for COVID was significantly associated with older age having been vaccinated for influenza last winter perceiving greater risk of COVID to people in the UK more positive general COVID vaccination beliefs and attitudes weaker beliefs that the vaccination would cause side effects or be unsafe greater perceived information sufficiency to make an informed decision about COVID vaccination and lower endorsement of the otion that only people who are at risk of serious illness should be vaccinated for COVID

In terms of explained variance the strongest predictors were the principal components representing general COVID vaccination beliefs and attitudes of variance explained followed n________________ was added it explained an additional of the variance

Adding general vaccination beliefs and attitudes block resulted in the largest increase in proportion of explained variance though in the full model the predictors in this group were o longer significant
When beliefs and atti tudes about COVID block were added to the model they explained more of the variance in vaccination intention

Adding positive beliefs and attitudes about COVID vaccination block explained further of the variance If COVID vaccination were to be offered to the general population one advantage might be the ability to achieve herd immunity
Information about herd immunity and vacci ation estimates are rapidly changing

While some estimates indicate that up to of the population might eed to be vaccinated to achieve this recent research suggests this per centage could be considerably lower depending on variation in intending to be vaccinated for COVID when vaccine becomes available to them

While intention is key driver of the uptake of health behaviors vaccination intention is likely to be greater than actual vaccine uptake Therefore it is important to identify factors associated with vaccination intention early on to support policy and communications when vaccine becomes available

We found that taken together about COVID and COVID vaccination explained of the variance in vaccination intention Importantly we found that the factor that explained the greatest proportion of the variance in vaccination intention was COVID vaccination beliefs and attitudes

This factor encompassed items measuring positive influence of recommendations from authorities to be vaccinated greater perceived social orms about vaccination greater perceived effectiveness greater perceived likelihood of catching COVID without vaccine greater anticipated regret of ot being vaccinated beliefs that COVID vaccination should be mandatory and greater perceived ease of vaccina tion

These map on to theoretical constructs of threat apprai sal coping appraisal subjective orms and self efficacy outlined by theories of uptake of health behaviors which were also associated with uptake of vaccination during the influenza pandemic Earlier research investigating COVID vaccine willingness in the UK found o associa tion with perceived likelihood of catching COVID trust in authorities or clarity of information about the virus However those earlier results should be interpreted with caution as analyses did ot control for personal or clinical characteristics and data were collected early in the pandemic
Our results suggest that people may hold general positive or egative beliefs and attitudes toward the vaccination and this general sense is driving vaccination intention at this point

While COVID vaccination has so far generally been positively framed in the media as more information and misinformation about the vaccine comes to light there is the potential for this general positive sentiment to be eroded egatively influencing vaccination intention and uptake

Since our survey was conducted the UK trial of coronavirus vaccine by the University of Oxford and AstraZeneca was halted for week in September n________________ following the adverse reaction of patient It is unclear what impact if any this might have on vaccination intentions and how long any impact might last

Regular and longitudinal assessments such as the one we report here can help clarify such impacts Details around COVID vaccination remain uncertain until vaccine has been developed but will become clearer as more information is available regarding vaccine composition immunogenicity and safety and immunity after having con tracted COVID We found that vaccination intention was associated with greater perceived information sufficiency about COVID and COVID vaccination
In the case of COVID perception of sufficient information about the vaccination is interesting as there is currently little such information available
What information there is comes from results of vaccine trials that were still underway at the time of data collection

These results may therefore reflect participants general vaccine beliefs and attitudes In contrast to previous research we found o evidence of an association between greater perceived risk of COVID to oneself and vaccination intention
However greater perceived risk to others was associated with vaccination intention in our study
This suggests that vaccination campaigns and messaging highlighting the eed for vaccination for altruistic reasons to protect others might be particularly effective
We also found that concerns about adverse effects and vaccine ovelty were associated with vaccination intention

As ovel threats are perceived as inherently more risky and perceiving adverse effects is consistently associated with vaccination refusal this is unsurprising Eligibility criteria for COVID vaccination are ot yet clear

Initial guidance from the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunization suggests that vaccination should be prioritized among frontline health and social care workers and those at increased risk of critical illness or death from COVID We found o evidence of an association between clinical vulnerability to COVID and vaccination intention
However vaccination intention was lower in those who thought that only those who are at risk of serious illness eed to be vaccinated
This may be because most of the sample did ot think that they were at increased clinical risk of COVID

Our finding that thinking that one has had COVID was ot associated with vaccination intention is reassuring With some evidence suggesting that repeated vaccination for COVID may be ecessary parallels with seasonal influenza vaccination can be drawn and lessons learned to promote vaccination uptake
Populations at greater clinical risk of serious illness from COVID are also similar to those at risk of serious illness from influenza and target populations for vaccines are likely to be similar
We found that seasonal influenza vaccination was strongly associated with COVID vaccination intention
Taken together these factors may suggest that in future years co administration of the seasonal influenza and COVID vaccines could be con sidered

In the meantime with the influenza season fast approaching in the UK at the time of writing and an increasing strain that concurrent circulation of seasonal influenza and COVID will put on healthcare services it is crucial that uptake of the seasonal influenza vaccine increases n________________ compared to uptake in England in year olds in clinical risk category in pregnant women and in pre school children and in school aged children Given the prominence of COVID in the media contextual factors are likely to be strongly influential in vaccination uptake with vaccine sentiments likely reflecting the media discourse
However there was o evidence for an association between beliefs about return to ormal and COVID vaccination intention using our stringent criteria for statistical significance
This may be due to the continuing uncertainties surrounding COVID vaccination

Given the potential for sensationalized stories to increase perceptions of the likelihood and severity of adverse effects decrease vaccine uptake and in some cases lead to political responses including the suspension of vaccination programs it is important that when more information about vaccine becomes available clear factual account is portrayed in the media

It remains to be seen how this might be implemented in practice In line with other research conducted on COVID vac cine willingness in the UK we found that older age was associated with greater intention to be vaccinated
This finding may reflect the related increased uptake of seasonal influenza vaccination in older age groups
It may also reflect the well publicized increased risk of COVID associated morbidity and mortality This study has limitations

First although we used demographically representative sample of the UK popula tion we cannot be sure how representative survey respon dents are of the views and behaviors of the general population However we assume that the associations between variables follow the same pattern as those in the general population Second we cannot infer causality due to the cross sectional ature of the study

Actual vaccination uptake is likely to be lower Given the theoretical importance of intention in theories of uptake of health behaviors it is likely that factors associated with vaccination intention in n________________ this study will also influence vaccination uptake
Fourth due to unclear evidence of the role of children in transmis sion of COVID in the UK and space constraints in the survey we chose ot to investigate intention to vaccinate one child for COVID
Future research could usefully consider the impact of any details that emerge about COVID vaccine such as how effective the vaccine is and how long immunity conferred by the vaccine lasts

It would also be useful to conduct age stratified research to further understand how beliefs such as personal risk per ception might vary and interact with intention to get vac cinated by age High levels of uptake of COVID vaccination when one becomes available will be ecessary in order for the UK gov ernment COVID recovery strategy to be fulfilled
To the best of our knowledge this is the first methodologically rigor ous study investigating the intention to receive COVID vaccination in demographically representative sample of the UK population
While there is still much uncertainty sur rounding COVID and vaccination results from this study provide useful insights that can help guide policy and commu ications when vaccine becomes available
The UK popula tion is still divided in their intention to be vaccinated for COVID
Approximately two thirds report being likely to be vaccinated when vaccine becomes available to them despite the dearth of information about COVID vaccina tion

As vaccine uptake is likely to be lower than vaccination intention it is worrying that the remaining third were unsure or did ot intend to be vaccinated for COVID given the impact of COVID on day to day life and prominence of the virus in the media
These findings are likely to reflect general vaccine attitudes and beliefs and clear information about the safety and effectiveness of the vaccine may be eeded to increase vaccination intentions
Our results indicate that vaccination campaigns and communications should draw on the oretical constructs
Contextual factors such as the media discourse around COVID vaccination are likely to influence beliefs and attitudes toward the vaccine

content The COVID pandemic has created the largest disruption of education systems in human history affecting early billion learners in more than countries
Closures of schools institutions and other learning spaces have impacted more than of the world student population
This has brought far reaching changes in all aspects of our lives
Social distancing and restrictive movement policies have significantly disturbed traditional educational practices

Reopening of schools after relaxation of restriction is another challenge with many ew standard operating procedures put in place Within short span of the COVID pandemic many researchers have shared their works on teaching and learning in different ways
Several schools colleges and universities have discontinued face to face teachings
There is fear of losing academic year or even more in the coming future
The eed of the hour is to innovate and implement alternative educational system and assessment strategies
The COVID pandemic has provided us with an opportunity to pave the way for introducing digital learning

This article aims to provide comprehensive report on the impact of the COVID pandemic on online teaching and learning of various papers and indicate the way forward The global outbreak of the COVID pandemic has spread worldwide affecting almost all countries and territories
The countries around the world cautioned the public to take responsive care
The public care strategies have included handwashing wearing face masks physical distancing and avoiding mass gathering and assemblies

Lockdown and staying home strategies have been put in place as the eeded action to flatten the curve and control the transmission of the disease Sintema Bhutan first declared closing of schools and institutions and reduction of business hours during the second week of March Kuensel March
In between movements were allowed offices began functioning schools and college reopened for selected levels and continued with online class for others
More than children in Bhutan from classes PP XII are today affected by the school closure
The impact is far reaching and has affected learning during this academic year or even more in the coming days
Several schools colleges and universities have discontinued face to face teaching
There is pressing eed to innovate and implement alternative educational and assessment strategies

The COVID pandemic has provided us with an opportunity to pave the way for introducing digital learning Dhawan Research highlights certain dearth such as the weakness of online teaching infrastructure the limited exposure of teachers to online teaching the information gap on conducive environment for learning at home equity and academic excellence in terms of higher education
This article evaluates the impact of the COVID pandemic on teaching and learning process across the world

The challenges and opportunities of online and continuing education during the COVID pandemic is summarized and way forward suggested Lockdown and social distancing measures due to the COVID pandemic have led to closures of schools training institutes and higher education facilities in most countries
There is paradigm shift in the way educators deliver quality education through various online platforms
The online learning distance and continuing education have become panacea for this unprecedented global pandemic despite the challenges posed to both educators and the learners

Transitioning from traditional face to face learning to online learning can be an entirely different experience for the learners and the educators which they must adapt to with little or o other alternatives available

The education system and the educators have adopted Education in Emergency through various online platforms and are compelled to adopt system that they are ot prepared for E learning tools have played crucial role during this pandemic helping schools and universities facilitate student learning during the closure of universities and schools
While adapting to the ew changes staff and student readiness eeds to be gauged and supported accordingly
The learners with fixed mindset find it difficult to adapt and adjust whereas the learners with growth mindset quickly adapt to ew learning environment
There is o one size fits all pedagogy for online learning
Different subjects and age groups require different approaches to online learning

Online learning also allows physically challenged students with more freedom to participate in learning in the virtual environment requiring limited movement As schools have been closed to cope with the global pandemic students parents and educators around the globe have felt the unexpected ripple effect of the COVID pandemic

While governments frontline workers and health officials are doing their best slowing down the outbreak education systems are trying to continue imparting quality education for all during these difficult times
Many students at home living space have undergone psychological and emotional distress and have been unable to engage productively

The best practices for online homeschooling are yet to be explored The use of suitable and relevant pedagogy for online education may depend on the expertise and exposure to information and communications technology for both educators and the learners

Some of the online platforms used so far include unified communication and collaboration platforms such as Microsoft Teams Google Classroom Canvas and Blackboard which allow the teachers to create educational courses training and skill development programmes
They include options of workplace chat video meeting and file storage that keep classes organized and easy to work
They usually support the sharing of variety of content like Word PDF Excel file audio videos and many more

These also allow the tracking of student learning and assessment by using quizzes and the rubric based assessment of submitted assignments The flipped classroom is simple strategy for providing learning resources such as articles pre recorded videos and YouTube links before the class
The online classroom time is then used to deepen understanding through discussion with faculty and peers
This is very effective way of encouraging skills such as problem solving critical thinking and self directed learning

The virtual classroom platforms like videoconferencing Google Hangouts Meet Zoom Slack Cisco WebEx and customizable cloud based learning management platforms such as Elias Moodle BigBlueButton and Skype are increasingly being used With the availability of sea of platforms and online educational tools the users both educators and learners face frequent hiccups while using it or referring to these tools

Some of the challenges identified and highlighted by many researchers are summarized as follows Broadly identified challenges with learning are accessibility affordability flexibility learning pedagogy life long learning and educational policy Murgatrotd
Many countries have substantial issues with reliable Internet connection and access to digital devices
While in many developing countries the economically backward children are unable to afford online learning devices the online education poses risk of exposure to increased screen time for the learner
Therefore it has become essential for students to engage in offline activities and self exploratory learning
Lack of parental guidance especially for young learners is another challenge as both parents are working

There are practical issues around physical workspaces conducive to different ways of learning The innately motivated learners are relatively unaffected in their learning as they eed minimum supervision and guidance while the vulnerable group consisting of students who are weak in learning face difficulties

Some academically competent learners from economically disadvantaged background are unable to access and afford online learning The level of academic performance of the students is likely to drop for the classes held for both year end examination and internal examination due to reduced contact hour for learners and lack of consultation with teachers when facing difficulties in learning understanding Student assessments are carried out online with lot of trial and error uncertainty and confusion among the teachers students and parents
The approach adopted to conduct online examination varies as per the convenience and expertise among the educators and the compatibility of the learners
Appropriate measures to check plagiarism is yet to be put in place in many schools and institutions mainly due to the large umber of student population

The lockdown of schools and colleges has ot only affected internal assessments and examinations for the main public qualifications like General Certificate of Secondary Educations GCSE but levels have also been cancelled for the entire cohort in the UK
Depending on the duration of the lockdown postponement or cancellation of the entire examination assessment might be grim possibility United Nations
Various state level board exams recruitment exams university level exams and entrance exams have been postponed across India due to the COVID outbreak and ational lockdown
Various entrance examinations such as BITSAT NATA CLAT MAT ATMA have also been postponed rescheduled

The education system in schools colleges and universities across the country has been severely impacted due to the ongoing situation It is also possible that some students careers might benefit from the interruptions
in Norway it has been decided that all grade students will be awarded high school degree

study carried out in France shows that the abandoning of the ormal examination procedures in France following the student riots led to positive long term labour market consequences for the affected cohort School time also raises social skills and awareness besides being fun for the children
There are economic social and psychological repercussions on the life of students while they are away from the ormal schedule of schools
Many of these students have ow taken online classes spending additional time on virtual platforms which have left children vulnerable to online exploitation
Increased and unstructured time spent on online learning has exposed children to potentially harmful and violent content as well as greater risk of cyberbullying

School closures and strict containment measures mean more families have been relying on technology and digital solutions to keep children engaged in learning entertained and connected to the outside world but ot all children have the ecessary knowledge skills and resources to keep themselves safe online In the case of online learning in Bhutan majority of the learners are from rural villages where parents are mostly illiterate farmers
Students are engaged in assisting parents in farm activities such as agriculture tending to cattle and household chores
